item.text:
## 1B.2 Evidence Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024

**Working judgment:** I found **clear pro-restraint / anti-brinkmanship evidence** and **no reliable 2024 evidence of Marcos using reckless nuclear rhetoric, apocalyptic language, or normalizing nuclear use**. The available record is mostly about **nuclear risk reduction and conventional security restraint**, not nuclear threats.

| ID | Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | Favorable | US, China must engage in meaningful dialogue to maintain strategic stability, limit nuclear arms build-up — PBBM | Philippine Information Agency / PCO | 2024-03-05 | https://pia.gov.ph/press-releases/us-china-must-engage-in-meaningful-dialogue-to-maintain-strategic-stability-limit-nuclear-arms-build-up-pbbm/ | Marcos explicitly called for strategic stability, limits on nuclear arms build-up, and broader nuclear-disarmament discussion. This is direct evidence of responsible nuclear rhetoric. | `1B.2`, `1B.1` |
| E2 | Favorable | PH, US, Japan affirm commitment to Korean Peninsula denuclearization, warn Russia on nuclear weapon use vs. Ukraine | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-12 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/ph-us-japan-affirm-commitment-to-korean-peninsula-denuclearization-warn-russia-on-nuclear-weapon-use-vs-ukraine/ | Marcos joined a trilateral statement affirming denuclearization and warning against nuclear weapon use in Ukraine. This is strong anti-brinkmanship evidence. | `1B.2`, `1B.1` |
| E3 | Favorable | Philippines not in business of instigating wars, says President Marcos | Reuters | 2024-06-23 | https://theprint.in/world/philippines-not-in-business-of-instigating-wars-says-president-marcos/2143467/ | Marcos said the Philippines is not in the business of instigating wars and would settle disputes peacefully. This is not nuclear language, but it supports a non-reckless escalation posture. | `1B.2`, `1B.1`, `7D.*` |
| E4 | Favorable / cautionary restraint | Marcos: Threat has grown, PH must do more to defend territory | GMA News Online / Reuters interview | 2024-03-19 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/901032/marcos-threat-has-grown-in-south-china-sea-philippines-must-do-more-to-defend-territory/story/owl.video.play.png | Marcos used firm security language about a growing South China Sea threat, but also said invoking the MDT would not serve a purpose unless the situation became “existential.” That is hawkish, but still bounded and not nuclear brinkmanship. | `1B.2`, `1B.1`, `7D.*` |
| E5 | Neutral context, not nuclear rhetoric | PH not going to war but beefing up AFP vs. external threats | Philippine News Agency | 2024-06-06 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1226375 | Marcos backed stronger conventional defense while saying the Philippines was not going to war. This is the closest 2024 “hard line” evidence I found, but it does **not** show nuclear normalization or apocalyptic rhetoric. | `1B.2`, `1B.1`, `7D.*` |

### Synthesis

- **Best evidence for 1B.2:** Marcos used explicit **anti-nuclear** and **anti-escalation** language in March and April 2024, including calls to limit nuclear arms build-up and support for denuclearization.
- **Best cautionary evidence:** He maintained a firm security posture on the South China Sea and external threats, but the language stayed within conventional deterrence and peace-restraint framing.
- **Search gap:** I did **not** find a reliable 2024 source showing Marcos himself making reckless nuclear threats, apocalyptic statements, or normalizing nuclear use. The search results repeatedly turned up the opposite: denuclearization, nuclear-risk reduction, and “settle disputes peacefully” language.

**Working judgment for 1B.2:** **Yes, on the evidence found.** Marcos’s 2024 rhetoric appears **responsible and restrained on nuclear issues**, with no credible evidence of nuclear brinkmanship.
